items.symptoms_en: Bored squares, flowers or bolls with feeding holes and larval frass.
items.damage_en: Flower and boll shedding, damaged lint and yield loss.
items.favourable_conditions_en: Continuous host availability and flowering to boll formation stage.
items.etl: Use local Department/PJTSAU ETL for current season.

recommendations.recommendation_en: Use timely sowing, avoid excess nitrogen, conserve natural enemies and remove damaged fruiting bodies where practical.
Use pheromone traps and need-based biological control as per official IPM package.
Official recommendation will be updated soon. Please follow local PJTSAU/Department advisory.

items.symptoms_en: Yellowing and curling of leaf edges, reddening and hopper burn in severe cases.
items.damage_en: Sap sucking weakens plants and reduces growth.
items.favourable_conditions_en: Warm dry weather and young crop stage.
items.etl: Use local Department/PJTSAU ETL for current season.

recommendations.recommendation_en: Avoid excess nitrogen and monitor underside of leaves regularly.
Official recommendation will be updated soon. Please follow local PJTSAU/Department advisory.

items.symptoms_en: Mixed weeds competing with cotton during early growth.
items.damage_en: Competition for moisture, nutrients and light.
items.favourable_conditions_en: Early monsoon flush and wide row spacing.

recommendations.recommendation_en: Keep crop weed-free during early growth using timely intercultivation and hand weeding.
Official recommendation will be updated soon. Please follow local PJTSAU/Department advisory.

items.symptoms_en: Nymphs and adults remain at the plant base. Infested patches show hopper burn, drying or lodging and may transmit grassy stunt, ragged stunt and wilted stunt.
items.damage_en: Sap sucking causes yellowing, drying, circular hopper-burn patches and lodging in severe infestation.
items.favourable_conditions_en: Close planting, excess nitrogen, standing dense crop canopy and poor water management favour hopper build-up.
items.etl: ETL: 1 hopper/tiller without predatory spider; 2 hoppers/tiller when spider is present.
items.source_name: TNAU Rice Crop Protection PWA Template

recommendations.recommendation_en: Avoid close planting, use alternate wetting and drying, avoid excess nitrogen and drain water before directing spray to the plant base when control is required.
Conserve predatory spiders and other natural enemies; use monitoring-based IPM before chemical control.
TNAU template notes neem oil/azadirachtin and listed insecticides, but dose must be verified against latest CIBRC label and PJTSAU/Telangana advisory before display.

items.symptoms_en: Dead heart in tillering stage and white ear at panicle stage. Affected shoots or panicles pull out easily.
items.damage_en: Central shoot dries during vegetative growth; panicles become white, chaffy and unfilled at reproductive stage.
items.favourable_conditions_en: Continuous rice cultivation, carry-over stubbles and favourable humid crop canopy.
items.etl: ETL: 10% dead heart or 2% white ear.
items.source_name: TNAU Rice Crop Protection PWA Template

recommendations.recommendation_en: Clip seedling tips, remove stubbles and install light or pheromone traps where recommended.
Release Trichogramma japonicum as per official IPM schedule and local advisory.
The template refers to neem products and listed insecticides; verify latest CIBRC label and PJTSAU/Telangana advisory before field recommendation.

items.symptoms_en: Larva folds leaves longitudinally and scrapes green tissue. Leaves turn white or dry; severe infestation gives a scorched field appearance.
items.damage_en: Reduced photosynthetic leaf area and drying of leaves, especially when flag leaves are damaged.
items.favourable_conditions_en: Excess nitrogen, dense canopy, weedy bunds and humid conditions favour leaf folder multiplication.
items.etl: ETL: 10% leaf damage at vegetative stage; 5% flag leaf damage at flowering.
items.source_name: TNAU Rice Crop Protection PWA Template

recommendations.recommendation_en: Avoid excess nitrogen and keep bunds clean to reduce pest carry-over.
Release Trichogramma chilonis as per official IPM schedule; use NSKE or azadirachtin where advised.
Verify current official insecticide and dose before app display or field use.

items.symptoms_en: Spindle-shaped grey lesions with brown margins; neck infection causes chaffy grains.
items.damage_en: Leaf blighting, neck break and grain loss.
items.favourable_conditions_en: Cloudy weather, high humidity and excess nitrogen.

recommendations.recommendation_en: Use clean seed, tolerant varieties where available and avoid excess nitrogen. Verify Telangana advisory before field recommendation.

items.symptoms_en: Stunted seedlings or plants, yellowing, patchy field growth, early maturity under heavy infestation, reduced tillers, smaller earheads, fewer grains and root tip or terminal galls.
items.damage_en: Reduced tillering, smaller earheads and fewer grains due to root damage and poor nutrient uptake.
items.favourable_conditions_en: Infested nursery or field soil and non-submerged conditions favour nematode damage.
items.etl: Refer latest nematode advisory and field diagnosis.

recommendations.recommendation_en: Keep rice flooded or submerged where appropriate and raise seedlings in flooded soils.
Rotate with non-host crops such as daincha and use soil solarization for nursery or field preparation where practical.
Verify any chemical seedling treatment against the latest label and local advisory before use.

items.symptoms_en: Mixed weed flora in nursery or transplanted/main field.
items.favourable_conditions_en: Poor puddling, gaps in stand and shallow water management.

recommendations.recommendation_en: Maintain proper puddling, plant spacing and timely hand weeding or cono weeding.

items.symptoms_en: Window panes and ragged leaf feeding; larvae and frass in whorl.
items.damage_en: Whorl damage, leaf shredding and yield reduction in severe infestation.
items.favourable_conditions_en: Warm weather and young maize crop.

recommendations.recommendation_en: Monitor whorls, destroy egg masses where feasible and remove severely damaged seedlings.
Use pheromone traps and biological options as per official IPM package.
Official recommendation will be updated soon. Please follow local PJTSAU/Department advisory.

items.symptoms_en: Weeds emerging with crop rows during first month.
items.damage_en: Strong competition for moisture and nutrients.
items.favourable_conditions_en: Rain after sowing and delayed intercultivation.

recommendations.recommendation_en: Keep field weed-free up to knee-high stage using intercultivation and hand weeding.

items.symptoms_en: Larva feeds with head inside pod; round holes on pods.
items.favourable_conditions_en: Flowering and podding stage with cloudy weather.

recommendations.recommendation_en: Install pheromone traps, conserve natural enemies and use need-based IPM.
